source_snapshot.procedure: Run raw 0x06/0x37 locally in-band and remotely over lanplus, record the response and compare it after firmware update.
source_snapshot.criteria: Command should be sent without any error; no length, identity, byte-order, cross-path or pre/post stability acceptance is supplied.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL incorrectly says exact request bytes are missing although the row supplies 0x06/0x37, but correctly requests expected output.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: FULLY AUTOMATABLE correctly requires 16-byte parsing and same-target baseline provenance, but makes the source-explicit OOB and post-firmware comparisons optional.

old_problem: The historical record retained Pending and Source Conflict because Criteria only checks command success while Procedure requires IB/OOB capture and post-firmware comparison. IPMI v2.0 section 22.14 defines no-data App 0x37 and exactly 16 opaque GUID bytes, recommends raw byte consistency with SMBIOS UUID and states identity must not change. The missing target and pre/post baseline are finite lifecycle inputs, not missing command semantics.
disposition_reason: Preserve both explicit IB and OOB reads and the required after-firmware comparison. Bind the same immutable asset/BMC, capture exactly 16 raw bytes on each path, compare them byte-for-byte to the raw SMBIOS Type 1 UUID when present, store an opaque canonical representation under a versioned rule, and require the post-update raw value to equal the approved pre-update baseline. This case performs no firmware update; without the separately approved post-update phase it records BASELINE CAPTURED, not PASS.
decision_basis: XLSX row 1011, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 1012 were directly reviewed; next pending was verified as Functionality row 1012 / variant d57b39b36131eb03.

IPMI v2.0 section 22.14 and Table 22-17 define App 0x37 with no request data and exactly 16 GUID response bytes after completion; the GUID is an opaque globally unique 128-bit number and must not change over device lifetime.

Section 22.14.1 prioritizes byte-for-byte alignment between the 16 IPMI bytes and SMBIOS UUID bytes in lowest-to-highest memory address order, regardless of sub-field ordering. Raw bytes are therefore the authoritative comparison; display canonicalization is secondary and versioned.

DMTF SMBIOS 3.8.0 Type 1 and section 7.2.1 define the raw 16-byte System UUID and its display byte order, and state all-FF or all-00 means the ID is not present. Such values cannot satisfy a valid GUID comparison.

The source explicitly requires IB, OOB and after-firmware comparison. A separately approved flash case owns update/downgrade and health coverage; this read-only case must retain the pre/post identity assertion without executing or inferring the update.

ED-02, ED-03, ED-07, ED-12, ED-13, ED-15 through ED-19, ED-22 and ED-28 preserve transport identity, flash-stage separation and evidence; ED-33 through ED-38 permit parameterized baselines while prohibiting log clear, target substitution or retry.

test_case.test_name: Verify System GUID byte identity across IB/OOB and a separately approved firmware transition
test_case.purpose: Prove the same physical system returns one valid, stable 16-byte System GUID through source-required in-band and OOB IPMI paths, matches the raw SMBIOS Type 1 UUID when present, and remains unchanged across the separately authorized firmware update without this case performing any mutation.
required_package: Immutable asset/serial/board identifiers binding host, BMC and local IPMI device, with pre/post firmware inventory and approved firmware-change transaction ID
Pinned ipmitool build and versioned App 0x37 parser that separates transport/completion, requires exactly 16 data bytes and preserves raw order
Pinned SMBIOS Type 1 raw-table parser and canonical UUID formatter implementing DMTF byte ordering while retaining raw 16-byte evidence
Protected same-BMC lanplus wrapper using secret-safe credential injection and identity verification; no plaintext password argument or target ambiguity
Signed/hashed pre-update baseline and post-update phase record containing both IB/OOB raw GUIDs, SMBIOS bytes, target/firmware provenance and no-write/no-clear/no-retry audit
test_case.test_command: READ-ONLY TWO-PHASE AUTOMATION ONLY; DO NOT RUN DURING REVIEW. Bind the exact asset, host, BMC and local IPMI device; preserve logs. In PRE_UPDATE or POST_UPDATE phase, record immutable asset and firmware identity, extract raw SMBIOS Type 1 UUID bytes in memory order if present, then issue the pinned local in-band equivalent of `ipmitool -I open -d <local-device> raw 0x06 0x37` once and the source-required protected same-BMC OOB equivalent of `ipmitool -I lanplus -H <BMC_IP> -U <BMC_USER> -E raw 0x06 0x37` once. Require successful transport/IPMI completion and exactly 16 data bytes per path. Reject all-zero/all-FF IPMI GUID and treat all-zero/all-FF SMBIOS as absent, not matching identity. Compare IB and OOB raw bytes exactly; when SMBIOS is present compare its raw 16 bytes exactly to IPMI before formatting. Store raw hex and a canonical UUID under the pinned DMTF formatter. PRE_UPDATE creates a hashed immutable baseline and returns BASELINE_CAPTURED/NOT_COMPLETE. Only POST_UPDATE associated with a separately approved successful firmware case compares same-asset raw IB/OOB/SMBIOS bytes with that baseline and may return PASS. Do not flash, reset, power cycle, clear logs, overwrite the baseline or retry automatically.
test_case.expected_result: In each phase, IB and OOB reach the same asset/BMC, complete 0x37 and return the same nonzero/non-FF 16 raw bytes; when SMBIOS UUID is present its raw memory-order bytes match exactly. In POST_UPDATE, the same raw GUID equals the immutable PRE_UPDATE baseline while firmware provenance reflects the approved transition. No logs or system state change. A PRE-only run is baseline captured, not PASS; proven unsupported is N/A only with platform SPEC.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires same immutable asset/BMC, both transport reads in both required phases, successful completion, exactly 16 valid raw bytes, IB/OOB equality, SMBIOS raw equality when present, pinned canonicalization and exact post-to-pre raw equality tied to a separately approved firmware transaction. Command success alone, canonical-string-only comparison, target/provenance mismatch, missing post phase, all-zero/all-FF IPMI value, raw-byte divergence, changed GUID, malformed length, credential exposure, log clear, baseline overwrite or retry cannot pass. Missing lifecycle inputs is NOT READY rather than Pending; unsupported is N/A only with SPEC proof.
safety_gate: Allow only read-only App NetFn 0x06 command 0x37 and SMBIOS table reads on verified identities; deny flash, reset, power, configuration and arbitrary raw commands.
Treat GUID bytes as opaque for the primary comparison. Do not infer a different identity by applying undocumented UUID field-endian transformations.
Bind IB and OOB to the same physical BMC and firmware; protect OOB secrets and prohibit plaintext password arguments or host-key bypass.
Preserve dmesg/syslog/SEL and all raw identity evidence. Do not perform the source's generic log-clear step.
Firmware update, downgrade and rollback remain separate explicitly approved cases with their own pre/post version and safety evidence; this case only consumes their transaction provenance.
Fail closed on timeout, wrong length, invalid/changed GUID, byte-order ambiguity or baseline mismatch; preserve evidence and do not retry or overwrite the baseline automatically.
expected_evidence: Asset/host/BMC/board identity, local device, firmware before/after and separate approved firmware transaction/health record
Pinned tool/parser/SMBIOS-formatter versions plus protected OOB policy and separate transport/IPMI completion records
Raw 16-byte IB, OOB and SMBIOS values for each phase, all-zero/all-FF checks and byte-for-byte parity results
Versioned canonical UUID display, immutable hashed PRE_UPDATE baseline and exact POST_UPDATE raw comparison
Preserved logs, no-flash/no-reset/no-power/no-write/no-clear/no-retry audit and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: No mutation is expected. On invalid, divergent or changed GUID, freeze the pre-update baseline, preserve all raw bytes, asset/firmware provenance and logs, close protected sessions and escalate to BMC/BIOS/platform owners. Do not rewrite GUID, roll firmware, flash, reset, power cycle, clear logs or repeat the read automatically. Any firmware recovery belongs to the separately approved update case.

source_conflict.reason: The Review layer retains the source's IB, OOB and post-firmware coverage but replaces command-success-only Criteria with authoritative 16-byte, raw SMBIOS, provenance and stability acceptance. Firmware mutation remains in a separate approved case rather than being silently dropped or executed here.

blocked.reason: Command, exact response length, raw comparison and SMBIOS alignment are authoritative. Target binding and pre/post firmware baseline provenance are finite lifecycle inputs for a read-only automated case.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Exact asset/host/BMC/local-device mapping; pinned tool/parser/SMBIOS formatter; protected OOB access; immutable pre-update baseline; post-update firmware transaction/provenance; timeout and evidence policy.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; REVIEW-LAYER READ-ONLY TWO-PHASE CASE ONLY; NO IPMI, SSH, LOG, FIRMWARE, RESET, POWER OR DUT COMMAND EXECUTED

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1
external_authorities.application: Sections 22.14/22.14.1, Tables 22-1/22-17 and Appendix G define optional App 0x37, exactly 16 opaque GUID bytes, lifetime stability and raw byte consistency with SMBIOS UUID.

external_authorities.title: DMTF SMBIOS Reference Specification DSP0134 v3.8.0
external_authorities.application: Type 1 and section 7.2.1 define the raw 16-byte System UUID, canonical byte-order convention and all-00/all-FF absent values used by the comparison parser.

project_authority: The Project owner binds the immutable asset/BMC, protected transports, parser versions and approved firmware transaction, and supplies the signed pre-update baseline. Those inputs cannot waive raw IB/OOB/SMBIOS equality, make a missing post-update phase PASS, authorize a flash in this case or overwrite a changed identity.
